name: Katherine Nielsen
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember returning somebody's wage slip in a blank envelope.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the corner outside Coastal Barber, where Katherine usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I found the wage slip on the pavement. I knew what it might cost him if the wrong friend saw it.
appearance: Katherine has a round face with a pronounced chin. Look for dark brown curls cut close behind the ears. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a faded indigo overshirt with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. In conversation Katherine rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Katherine is kind in very practical ways and prickly about being thanked in public. Katherine loves being recognized by the people who notice what happens after the guests have left.
agenda: To return the wage slip directly to its owner.
family: Dora Frost is Katherine’s cousin. Katherine puts the kettle on. Dora chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *A room above the dryers*, Dora says, “I draw the people who wait for their washing and forget what their own faces are doing.”
connections: Ansel Perry. An old window bill and a found wage slip bring the young worker's finances into two households.

reactions.situation: An old customer arrives during the new warehouse shift
reactions.response: Katherine asks the two people to talk away from the work floor and leaves disclosure to the new hire.

reactions.situation: Smoke appears under a shop door after closing
reactions.response: Katherine alerts the nearest occupied shop, stays outside and writes down when the smoke first appeared.
